conviction_note: Q3 2026 had no US hurricane landfall (Isaias on Oct 9 was the first since Milton 2024), Heritage issued no preliminary Q3 cat release, the June 2026 reinsurance program cuts about $15.8M pre-tax of ceded cost from each full quarter, and peer Universal printed $1.93 adj. EPS against a $1.08 consensus. Taken together these point to EPS near $1.8-2.0 against a $0.77-$1.07 consensus. This name has rallied +12 to +18% on each of its last three beats and fell -20% on its one miss. abs_move 14.5 comes from the baseline's 14.47 median because no option chain is usable. p_up 60 rather than 65+ because the three estimate sources disagree (lesson 6, core table), Q2's $23.4M favourable reserve release flatters the Q2 run-rate, and the stock fell 5.9% in the five sessions after Universal's beat, which suggests a beat is partly expected. The findings sum to +4.1 and the scaled number is +2.9; the gap is the disputed bar and the post-UVE drift, which move p_up rather than the individual findings.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus is disputed across three sources that do not agree: Yahoo three-analyst average $0.77 (range $0.58-$1.07, captured 2026-09-25, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HRTG/analysis/); Benzinga $0.83 with revenue $217.0M, updated 2026-09-30 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HRTG/earnings-forecasts); Earnings Whispers $1.07 with revenue $220.08M (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/hrtg). Sized against the highest, $1.07; my read is EPS of about $1.85, which gives +73% (+120% against $0.83). The company gives no numeric guidance (Q2 release, https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/heritage-insurance-holdings-heritage-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-20260805). Because the bar is disputed, every finding is capped per lesson 6. Revenue bar about $217-220M, expected roughly in line.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was catastrophe-free for Heritage's footprint. Isaias (Oct 9 landfall, Destin) was the first continental US hurricane since Milton in 2024, so no hurricane hit inside Jul-Sep, and Heritage issued no preliminary Q3 cat/weather release, which it did issue in a heavy quarter (Oct 2020). The closest analog, Q3 2025 (zero cat losses, $13.8M weather, $5M favourable development), printed $1.63 against a $0.53 Zacks consensus. The Q3 2026 bar is $0.77-$1.07.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS surprise is the line this stock trades on: Q3 2025 $1.63 vs $0.53 consensus +12.48%; Q4 2025 beat +17.90%; Q2 2026 $2.05 vs $0.99 +16.47%; Q1 2026 $1.19 vs about $1.56 (miss) -20.05% (baseline history; Zacks https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2786207/heritage-insurance-hrtg-q3-earnings-and-revenues-top-estimates; Earnings Whispers https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/HRTG).
findings.why_not_priced: Every consensus source still sits at $0.77-$1.07, roughly half of the Q3 2025 analog, which implies a cat load analysts have not removed (Yahoo and Benzinga snapshots are dated late September, before the quarter's weather was fully known). Had it been priced, the stock would have re-rated after Universal's Oct 22 beat. Instead it fell 5.9% over five sessions.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 analog from Heritage's own 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1598665/000119312525267080/d768057dex991.htm). Gallagher Re: nine-month 2026 global insured cat losses the lowest since 2019 (via Insurance Business search result). Heritage's 2020 practice of pre-announcing Q3 cat losses: https://www.heritagepci.com/investor-news/heritage-announces-preliminary-third-quarter-2020-catastrophe-and-weather-losses/

findings.finding: Heritage's June 2026 CAT XOL program costs $367.5M, $63.2M less than the prior year, with seven-twelfths ($36.9M) recognised in 2026. That is about $15.8M pre-tax (about $0.40 per diluted share after tax) of lower ceded premium in each full quarter, and Q3 is the first full quarter (Q2 carried one month). The Q2 ceded ratio was already down to 42.7% from 44.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history. The Q2 2026 release that first quantified the saving coincided with +16.47%. Universal's ceded ratio fell 5.1 points on its own new program in Q3 and helped its EPS beat (https://www.reinsurancene.ws/universals-q326-revenues-rise-9-6-to-439m/).
findings.why_not_priced: The saving is public, but a sub-$1.07 consensus is hard to reconcile with $0.40 a share of known cost relief on top of a $1.63 zero-cat analog, unless analysts carry a large cat load. If they had flowed it through, Q3 estimates would sit at or above Q3 2025's $1.63.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 release confirms the $63.2M and the 7/12 recognition (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/heritage-insurance-holdings-heritage-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-20260805). Shares no document with the weather finding.

findings.finding: Peer Universal Insurance (UVE, Florida homeowners, same June 1 reinsurance cycle) reported Q3 2026 on Oct 22, after Heritage last spoke: adjusted EPS $1.93 vs a $1.08 consensus (+79%), GAAP net income +31.8%, combined ratio 91.0% vs 96.4%, ceded premium ratio 27.6% vs 32.7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of HRTG reacting to UVE prints found. HRTG has fallen 5.92% in the five sessions since UVE reported (baseline run_up_5d).
findings.why_not_priced: HRTG consensus ($0.77-$1.07) shows no sign of being revised after the peer print, and HRTG traded down afterwards. If the read-through were priced, HRTG would have risen with it. The counterweight is that this public print may already have lifted the whisper number, so this finding is sized small.
findings.independence: UVE consensus $1.08 from Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/UVE/earnings-forecasts). Corroborates the quiet-quarter finding through a different company's audited numbers; same underlying weather fact, so sized small to avoid double counting.

findings.finding: Isaias, the Q4 event the call will be asked about, looks contained for Heritage. Florida OIR showed $582M insured and 46,509 claims as of Oct 15, 79% of them in Santa Rosa and Escambia; trade press reported 'fewer claims than expected'; Universal said claims were 'less significant than initially anticipated'. Heritage's Southeast retention is about $50M per first event, under a $1.865B tower, with only 112K Florida policies. Any Q4 estimate given on the call should fall well inside the retention.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024 (Helene/Milton) was a cat quarter; the baseline does not isolate the reaction to a forward storm estimate. No direct history.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is 7.5% below its high and fell 5.9% in the last five sessions, so some storm overhang may sit in the price. A Q4 net estimate well below the $50M retention removes it. If Isaias were fully priced as small, the post-landfall drawdown would have reversed.
findings.independence: Claims Journal / Insurance Journal: 'fewer claims than expected' (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/southeast/2026/10/13/888686.htm). Universal Q3 release comment (UVE 8-K above). Retention from the Heritage 2026-27 program release (https://investors.heritagepci.com/2026-05-28-Heritage-Announces-Full-Placement-of-2026-2027-CAT-XOL-Reinsurance-Program). Heritage's own Panhandle exposure was not found.

findings.finding: The top line is shrinking. Q2 2026 GPW was -5.5% ($388.4M), YTD -4.1%; policies in force -5.2%; Florida policies down to 112,304 from 241,581 in 2021; an average 3.3% Florida rate cut became effective Feb 18, 2026. Management said in May that full-year written premiums would turn positive, which needs a sharp second-half turn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 miss (-20.05%) came with underwriting and growth questions. In Q2 2026, GPW -5.5% did not stop a +16.47% reaction when EPS doubled consensus.
findings.why_not_priced: The May promise that full-year premiums turn positive (Seeking Alpha summary) is still on the table. A Q3 GPW print that is still negative would show it slipping and could cap the multiple, which at about 1.8x Q2 book already prices growth.
findings.independence: May 2026 call summary: 62.7% new-business growth, full-year GPW expected positive (https://seekingalpha.com/news/4590116-heritage-outlines-62_7-percent-new-business-growth-as-it-anticipates-full-year-written). Rate decrease (https://investors.heritagepci.com/2025-12-4-Heritage-Insurance-Announces-Approved-Rate-Decrease-up-to-Nearly-10-for-Property-and-Casualty-Insurance-Policyholders-in-Florida). Florida policy count (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/southeast/2026/08/10/880894.htm). Shares the Q2 release with the reserve finding.

findings.finding: Q2 2026's $2.05 included $23.4M of favourable prior-year reserve development (about $0.58 a share after tax), against $5M in Q3 2025. A Q3 with normal development has less cushion, and Q1 2026's miss shows the downside when the cushion is absent.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the low consensus already assumes much less than Q2. Filed because it is the main way the beat could come in smaller than the analog implies.
findings.independence: Same Q2 release as the top-line finding (one document, two different lines). Q3 2025 development of $5M from the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1598665/000119312525267080/d768057dex991.htm).

findings.finding: Capital return optionality: the dividend is suspended with the board 'reassessing each quarter', a new $50M buyback was authorised May 7, 2026 on top of $37.4M remaining, and management says it is generating substantial excess capital (Q2 book value per share $19.09, +54.5% year on year). A reinstated dividend or an accelerated buyback could come with the release.
findings.why_not_priced: Speculative; no announcement has been made. Sized small.
findings.independence: Insurance Journal on buybacks and excess capital (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/southeast/2026/08/10/880894.htm).

lessons_applied: Lesson 6 / core table, disputed bar: the three consensus sources ($0.77, $0.83, $1.07) do not agree, so the bar-dependent findings were capped: quiet quarter +4.0 to +3.0, reinsurance saving +1.5 to +1.0, and p_up 63 to 60.

'What has worked' (a peer's print landing after the company last spoke, leaving consensus stale): the Universal read-through raised from +0.5 to +0.8, kept small because it shares the weather fact with the first finding.

Lesson 7: short interest checked (2.4 days to cover, not crowded); the negatives are left as sized.
